_comment: Single source of truth for what the uptime probes check.
Read by scripts/uptime_probe.py, which is run by BOTH the GitHub Actions
cron and the Railway cron service. Previously each tool kept its own
hardcoded list, which is how 'webapp' silently went unmonitored after it
was deployed as its own service. Add a service here and every probe picks
For primary service probes, `name` should match the Railway SERVICE name so
scripts/status.py can join the URL onto control-plane service state. Extra
synthetic checks may use a descriptive suffix (for example terminal-contract);
the unattended uptime probe will execute them while status.py simply ignores
the unmatched synthetic name for control-plane joining.
`expect_contains` is a lightweight response-contract assertion. Every listed
marker must appear in the successful response body; this catches a proxy that
returns SPA HTML with HTTP 200 or an API route that silently changes shape.
Services with no public URL (python-worker, suwappu-relayer) cannot be
probed over HTTP at all — they are covered by the Railway deploy webhook
and by `python3 scripts/status.py`, which reads the control plane.
